Account Pre-Hijacking via Anonymous Orders and Gift CardsEditable vector diagram showing the legitimate user flow, account pre-hijacking attack flow, and password-verification mitigation.Account Pre-Hijacking via Anonymous Orders & Gift CardsMerging anonymous orders & gift cards into an attacker-controlled accountLEGITIMATE USER1User places ordersor uses gift cardsas a guestguest@example.com2User creates anaccount with thesame emailguest@example.com3Saleor sendsaccount confirmationlink to the email4User clicks theconfirmation link5Saleor merges existingorders & gift cardsinto the new accountLEGITIMATE OUTCOMEUser gains access to theirorder history and gift cardsin their account.Objects associated:OrdersGift cardsAddressesOther account dataATTACKER (ACCOUNT PRE-HIJACKING)1Attacker creates anaccount using thevictim's emailvictim@example.comAttacker sets a passwordcontrolled by them2Saleor sendsaccount confirmationlink to the victimvictim@example.com3Attacker tricks orinduces the victim toclick the linke.g. fake email creatingcuriosity or urgency4
id="path73" /> Victim clicks the confirmation link (thinking it's legitimate)5Saleor merges existingorders & gift cardsinto the attacker'saccount6Attacker logs in withtheir password andgains accessAccess to victim's orders, gift cards, and dataATTACKER OUTCOMEAttacker gains unauthorizedaccess to the victim’sorders, gift cards, andpersonal data.Impact:• Order history leakage• Gift card balance theft• Personal data exposure• Account takeoverMITIGATION IN SALEORSaleor requires passwordverification when confirmingan account.confirmAccount(email: <their-email>,password:<their-password>)The user must provide theaccount password whenconfirming.Victim doesn't know theattacker's password andcannot confirm the account.Victim must reset theirpassword, preventing theattacker from gaining access.Knowing the email and clicking the link is not enough to activate an account whose password is controlled by an attacker.
